item.description:

The post Fall Leaf Collection begins on October 13 appeared first on Village of Rye Brook.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Residents,

Beginning Tuesday, October 13, 2026, and continuing through to third week of December, the Village’s Highway Department will be collecting curbside leaves.  It is the Village’s goal to provide leaf collection service with a maximum of three (3) weeks between collections at peak periods (weather depending).   During the 12 to 13 week program season, highway department employees travel each street of the Village and collect leaves placed curbside. 

For equipment to be efficient, leaf piles need to place din a windrow along the curb line NOT in the roadway. Please advise your contractors not to create mounds of leaves at the curb, over storm drains or in the roadway, create long windrows.

The Village highway department methodically collects leaves according to a route system that essentially divides the Villages into thirds using the major roadways and balancing the historic leaf volume between neighborhoods.   Each route is covered with a team, consisting of three to four employees and the leaf collection equipment.  Trucks are not rerouted for any reason. The Village tracks the daily leaf collection street by street and monitors progress against the program goal. Such information can be found on the village’s website which is routinely updated. Please note the anticipated collection dates are approximate and subject to change.

A successful leaf collection program requires the cooperation of Village residents and the lawn care professionals residents may employ.  Branches, sticks, and other lawn debris, including stones, used planting pots, toys, broken lawn furniture, fence posts, and other non-leafy material must be kept out of the piles.  These materials can be drawn into the leaf equipment and cause serious injury to the workers and require costly repair to the equipment. Contaminants within and on top of leaf piles only slows down collection for you and your neighbors.

Residents are required to comply with the following:

  • Leaves must be placed in a tight row, a maximum of 4 feet wide, along the center of the curb line.  Rows shall not extend further than 2 feet into any roadway.
  • Leaf rows must be free of branches, logs, rocks, grass, plastics and other yard debris.
  • DO NOT place piles of leaves in the street, it is unsafe for motorists and slows down leaf removal. Violations and or summonses WILL be issued as a result.
  • Any questions: Please view the web page on “The Right and Wrong Way to Pile Leaves.”

Leaf piles with significant amounts of contaminants will not be removed until nonorganic debris and branches are removed. Leaves placed in plastic bags will not be removed. Residents are urged to review the Village website periodically, which will be updated with new information once leaf season kicks off.

Residents are urged to review the village website periodically, which will be updated with new information once leaf season begins.

Should you have any questions or comments please feel free to contact Village staff at 914 –939 -0753

Sincerely,
Michal J. Nowak
Superintendent of Public Works

https://ryebrookny.gov/leaf-collection/

item.content:encoded:
NEW ‘No Left Turns’ at BMP Ridge Street School M-F, 2:00-3:30PM:
The Village of Rye Brook and the Blind Brook School District have worked together to come up with ways to improve the traffic flow on North Ridge Street during school pickup times at the Bruno M. Ponterio (BMP) Ridge Street School. This has been a problem in the past school year when vehicles stop in both directions on the street waiting for dismissal and impeding traffic flow, making it difficult for emergency vehicles to get through the area.

Change Now in Effect: From Monday to Friday on school days, No Left Turns will be allowed into the middle and northern parking lots of the elementary school between 2:00pm and 3:30pm when travelling northbound. Also, when leaving these parking lots, only Right Hand Turns will be allowed. Only school buses will be exempt from these prohibited turns. The desired result will be maintaining traffic flow going northbound, and having vehicles queue up in only one direction travelling southbound making right-hand turns only which are much safer and more efficient.
Several Suggested Routes to get to the BMP Ridge Street School:

Parents and caregivers picking up students are urged to consider new travel routes to the school and to be respectful of the area neighbors by avoiding making U-turns on side streets or turning around in driveways.

Several possible routes are suggested below for student pickups during this restricted time period of 2:00pm to 3:30pm:

Route A: Travel north on Ridge Street and make a left turn onto Rockinghorse Trail. Make a right turn onto Dorchester and then another right turn onto Sleepy Hollow Road. Make a right turn onto Ridge Street before arriving at the Ridge Street School. Please click here for travel route video.

Route B: Travel north on Ridge Street past the Ridge Street School. Make a left turn onto Fairlawn Parkway, then a left turn onto Boxwood Place and a quick left turn onto Lawridge Drive to the end of the road. Make a left turn onto Sleepy Hollow and a right turn onto Ridge Street before arriving at the Ridge Street School. Please click here for travel route video.

Route C: Travel north on Ridge Street and go north on the Hutch Pkwy. Go under the King Street bridge and take the 1st exit where you make a right turn onto King Street and then a left turn onto Ridge Street before arriving at the Ridge Street School. Please click here for travel route video. IMPORTANT: IF THE PARKWAY EXIT RAMP IS BACKED UP TO THE PARKWAY, DO NOT QUEUE UP ON THE HUTCH/MERRIT PARKWAY- GO TO THE NEXT EXIT ON THE MERRIT PARKWAY AND TURN AROUND.]

Route D: Travel east on Betsy Brown Road and make a left onto King Street. Follow King Street and make a left turn onto Ridge Street before arriving at the Ridge Street School. Please click here for travel route video.

Route E: Travel south on King Street and make a right turn onto Ridge Street to Ridge Street School. No video to be added since no changes to this traffic pattern.

Police Officers will be present during the beginning of the school year to assist in the new traffic patterns, and the impact of these changes will continue to be monitored.
If you live in the Country Ridge neighborhood and want to share your experiences with these traffic changes after they are in effect, or would like to participate in a focus group on this subject, please email the Village (address removed from the fixture) . We ask that you please give it several months for new traffic patterns to form as parents adjust to these changes. The Village Board has said they will check in on the status of these changes in no more than three (3) months’ time.

item.content:encoded:
The Village of Rye Brook’s contractor continues the milling and paving Ridge Street from the Hutch Parkway bridge to Westchester Avenue. Please also be aware that temporary access to driveways (as the contractor passes by milling and paving), temporary stoppages of traffic, and possibly periodic detours may occur so motorists may want to consider alternate routes. The village asks for your patience and to provide additional time when travelling on Ridge Street. During any road resurfacing, motorists are also advised to be aware of elevated sewer drains and storm drains and use caution when driving over milled roads. Reduced speeds are also strongly recommended as these elevated structures may damage tires. Please do not drive on newly paved surfaces unless signaled. Please visit www.ryebrookny.gov regularly for any updates to the paving schedule, detour information, etc. One addition to Ridge Street will be a new crosswalk at Crawford Park. This crosswalk will be activated through a pedestrian push button when people are crossing.
